scenario: AITA for telling my mom she was a bad mother? | So this is kind of a two part thing. A while back, I made my mother upset because of a couple different things I said while out with her. She was saying something about how she didn't believe in doctors and that my siblings literally beg her to go and she still puts off taking them as long as possible. I told her that's not okay, that she did that to me and I nearly died (I was hospitalized for weeks, and spent several months on bedrest recovering), and that if she keeps that up one of us really might die some day because of her. She didn't take that too well, but ended up dropping it and brushing it off as no big deal. Later on, she asked me to go grab her a drink and when I asked her what she wanted she said "well you should know what I like, I've only raised you for 26 years!" And I told her no, I do not know what you like, my grandparents raised me, I still don't know anything about you. She got upset and started crying and said "what's your problem!? This is the second time today that you've been mean to me and tried to make me seem like a bad person!" I told her I'm not trying to be mean I was just saying it's not cool to not take your kid to the doctor and that I'm not going to know anything about her since I didnt grow up with her. We ended up going home shortly after and went out again the other night, a few weeks later. Well I got my brother a phone because they kept taking his (that a different family member pays for) and I wanted him to have his own, so I made it clear they can keep his other one and this one is STRICTLY for him. Well I found out they've been taking and using this one too, so when I saw her I told her, seriously, I dont want to take the phone back because I don't want him to be punished for what you're doing, but I will take it back if you don't stop stealing it from him. That is HIS that I'M paying for, not you, it is not yours to touch, it's already bad enough that you keep all his work money at least don't touch his phone. She got upset and starting yelling and crying saying I need to stop treating her like a bad mother, and I told her well to be honest she kind of IS one. She had a meltdown and started sobbing and said well fine, I don't need you in my life anyways, and left without me. Now my family is saying I shouldn't of treated her like that even if she wasn't that great to me. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to tell my mom that she's a bad mother. Let me start by understanding the situation better. From what I gather, there are a few things that happened: 1. **Belief in Doctors**: My mom doesn't believe in doctors, and even though my siblings begged her to take them, she put it off as long as possible. I was hospitalized for weeks and had to spend several months on bed rest recovering because of this. I told her that's not okay and that if she keeps doing that, one of us might die someday. She didn't take it well but eventually dropped it. 2. **Knowing What I Like**: She asked me to get her a drink and said, "Well, you should know what I like, I've only raised you for 26 years!" I responded that I don't know what she likes because my grandparents raised me and I still don't know anything about her. She got upset and cried, saying I was trying to make her seem like a bad person. 3. **Phone Situation**: I got my brother a phone because they kept taking his (paid for by a different family member). I made it clear they can keep his other one, but this one is strictly for him. I found out they've been taking and using this one too. I told her I don't want to take the phone back because I don't want him to be punished, but I will if she doesn't stop stealing it. She got upset, yelling and crying, saying I shouldn't treat her like a bad mother. I told her honestly that she kind of is. She had a meltdown, said she doesn't need me in her life, and left without me. Now, my family is saying I shouldn't have treated her like that, even if she wasn't that great to me. So, is it right or wrong for me to tell my mom she's a bad mother? First, I need to think about what defines a "bad mother." Generally, a good parent provides safety, support, guidance, and love. From the situation, it seems like my mom didn't take me to the doctor when I needed it, which put my health at risk. That's a serious issue because it shows a lack of responsibility and care. Also, the phone situation shows a pattern of behavior where she's taking things that belong to my brother, which is not appropriate. It seems like she's not respecting boundaries or acknowledging that the phone is for him, not for her to use. When I told her she's a bad mother, I was expressing my frustration and hurt about her actions. However, calling someone a bad parent can be hurtful and might not be the best way to communicate my feelings. It could escalate the situation and lead to more conflict. On the other hand, I have a right to express my feelings and set boundaries, especially when my well-being and my brother's well-being are at stake. It's important to stand up for ourselves and not tolerate harmful behavior. But I also need to consider the impact of my words. While it's valid to feel upset and to want to address her behavior, labeling her as a bad mother might not be the most constructive approach. It could make her defensive and less likely to listen to my concerns. Maybe instead of calling her a bad mother, I could have expressed how her actions have affected me and my brother, and how I would like things to change. This way, I'm addressing the behavior without attacking her as a person. However, I also need to acknowledge that she might not be open to hearing this, especially if she's defensive or unwilling to change. In that case, setting boundaries and protecting myself and my brother might be the healthier choice, even if it means reducing contact with her. In the end, it's a tough situation. I have to balance expressing my feelings and protecting myself with maintaining a relationship with my mom. It's not easy, and there's no perfect answer, but I need to do what feels right for me and my well-being.
